summary: Tested the Daily Ops Digest, admin re-ordering with the driver 'route updated' alert, nearby alerts/SMS and the Merchant CSV import, on the backend and on the frontend (390x844). Backend: new suite tests/test_digest_reorder_nearby_merchant.py has 19/19 passing. The full regression run (-n 0) had 114/115 passing. The one failure was a test-ordering problem in my own new test, which I fixed and re-ran (19/19). Frontend: every requested flow worked. Digest day picker with today, yesterday and 22 THU (late, complaints and failed lists shown). Admin move-down showed the 'MANUAL OVERRIDE · SEQUENCE SAVED · DRIVER NOTIFIED' toast. Driver banner appeared and GOT IT hid it (still hidden after reload). Customer banners: YOU'RE NEXT, 1 STOP AWAY and 2 STOPS AWAY. tracking-nearby-sms showed only when the status was forced to 'sent' in the DB. Merchant flow: home -> list -> mer-1, upload through the file chooser, progress reached 3/3, flagged rows 3 and 4, fix & retry created an MC order, a bogus address kept the error, REMOVE dropped the row, tapping an order opened /customer/MC...; bad-column CSV and .txt files each showed an error toast. No deprecated Expo packages found. A real 'sent' Twilio SMS was NOT tested because no real phone number was available.

minor.issue: Two resets at the same time return 500: E11000 duplicate key on code_redemptions.code (seed is not atomic). Seen when pytest-xdist runs 2 workers that each reset in a module fixture. Run the suite with -n 0 or make seeding idempotent.

process_import runs as a bare asyncio.create_task with no reference kept (it can be garbage-collected), and nothing recovers it after a backend restart. A job can then stay 'running' forever, and the UI disables merchant-upload-button whenever a job is running, which would block uploads for good.

A stop claimed as 'sending' stays 'sending' forever if send_nearby_sms crashes before its final update (for example, the process restarts). Also, PUT /api/stops/{id}/phone does not reset nearby_sms_status, so a stop already marked skipped_fictional never gets the text after a real number is set.

integration_issues.issue: The driver screen does not use the backend's /ws/route broadcast. It polls /drivers/{id}/route every 15s when GPS is off, so the banner can take up to 15s to appear after the admin re-orders (observed in roughly 8-20s).

issues: move-up/move-down arrows are 44x36, below the 44pt minimum height
Toast sits over the totals strip (ORDERS/ON THE WAY/DELIVERED/TO FIX) for its whole duration

action_items: Optional: subscribe the driver screen to /api/ws/route/{id} (or shorten polling) so the route-updated banner appears right away
Make import jobs survive a restart: on startup, mark stale 'running' jobs and re-queue their 'queued' rows, and keep a reference to the background task
Reset nearby_sms_status to null when the customer phone changes; clean up stuck 'sending' statuses
Make seed/reset safe to run concurrently (upsert or drop before insert)
Raise the reorder arrow height to 44
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is about 2,000 lines; split it into routers (digest, merchants/import, routes, contact)
geocode() appends ', San Francisco, CA, USA' even when the address already contains San Francisco (harmless, but the query is duplicated)
Driver alert depends on polling, not on the existing websocket broadcast

success_rate.backend: 100% (115/115 after fixing a test-ordering issue in my test)

seed_data_creation: Imported test rows (TEST_*/UI_*) on mer-1, then called POST /api/admin/reset at the end, so the DB is back to the clean seed with no imports. Geocode cache (db.geocodes) kept: 1 Market St, 450 Golden Gate Ave, and the bogus addresses are cached.
context_for_next_testing_agent: pytest.ini forces -n 2; run with -n 0 because module fixtures reset concurrently and then return 500. Backend env var is EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL. The FixRowSheet slide animation needs about 1.5s before its buttons can be clicked. The template button opens a CSV download popup that never fires load. Active route for drv-1 is found via GET /api/drivers/drv-1/route; nearby statuses are set on the first broadcast after reset (any reorder or simulate-step).
